item.title: Local TD calls for more affordable childcare & fair funding for rural services
item.description: A local TD has called for more affordable childcare and funding that supports rural as well as urban services. Roscommon-Galway TD Michael Fitzmaurice told the Dáil that current regulations have driven childminders out of the sector. He said there's huge pressure on crèches, where strict staff-to-child ratios and poor financial returns discourage providers from taking very young children. The Independent Ireland TD says demand has surpassed capacity even in the countryside: Advertisement

item.title: Eight IPAS centres currently open in the Shannonside region
item.description: There are currently 8 IPAS centres operating in the Shannonside region. The figures were released by the Justice Minister following a parliamentary question in the Dáil this week. As of January 25th, there are four IPAS centres open in Co. Roscommon. There are also two centres in both Longford and Leitrim. Justice Minister Jim O'Callaghan also provided figures on the amount of people staying in each county as of January 18th. There are 211 people currently staying in IPAS centres in Co. Leitrim.

item.title: Local Senator says use of AI is an opportunity Ireland can't afford to miss
item.description: A local Senator has said the use of artificial intelligence is an opportunity Ireland cannot afford to miss. Roscommon-Galway Senator Gareth Scahill says that AI regulation and innovation can and must coexist. The Fine Gael representative says Ireland is well positioned to lead in AI but must embed it into education and lifelong learning to build workforce capability. Senator Scahill says it can be a great tool if used correctly: Advertisement

item.title: End of an era as Boyle Post Office set to move location
item.description: The retiring postmaster of Boyle Post Office will turn the lights off on the premises for the final time this evening. Paul Forde has worked at the Shop Street location for 30 years, serving 18 of those as postmaster. Customers have been wishing him well throughout the day as the service moves to the Kelly's Supervalu Shopping Centre in the town from next Tuesday. item.title: More than letters and parcels: Paul Forde’s last day at Boyle Post Office
item.description: After three decades of service to the town, today marks the end of an era at Boyle Post Office. Paul Forde is retiring from his role as postmaster, closing the door on a career that has made him one of the town’s most familiar faces. The building has stood on Shop Street for over 100 years. Advertisement Paul Henry Kelly of Kelly's SuperValu will become the town's new postmaster, with the new premises to open on Tuesday next, February 3rd. item.title: 55 People Registered as Homeless in Shannonside Region Last Month
item.description: 55 people registered as homeless in the Shannonside region last month. The Department of Housing says there were 20 in Longford, 19 in Roscommon and 16 in Leitrim. item.title: Contingency Plan for Leopardstown Saturday January 31
item.description: Following an inspection earlier today, the course at Leopardstown was found to be fit for racing. However, with the possibility of 10-20mm (approx) of rain forecast for tonight, there will be a further inspection of the course tomorrow, Saturday, at 8am. This will determine whether this meeting can go ahead as scheduled.
